title: The Royal Hajj reaches Makka and the Kaʿba. The amir distributes gold freely, that no pilgrim there go hungry, and remains in the holy city for the pilgrimage itself, the days of Dhū al-Ḥijja at the end of January, before turning for home

data.choice: Distribute gold freely. Let no pilgrim here go hungry.
data.chronicleNote: The game resumes the expedition at once; the chronicle has him stay about a month for the rites (8–13 Dhū al-Ḥijja 752, about 26–31 January 1352 by the tabular calendar)

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, with the chosen option's tooltip open (game date 1 January 1352); the month in Makka is Trent's direction

title: The Hall of the Ambassadors: within the great tower of the palace on the Sabīka, the regent Faraj raises a throne hall to receive the envoys of kings, its cedar ceiling carved with the seven heavens above the throne

data.choice: Raise the hall and seat our throne beneath it.

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, with the chosen option's tooltip open

title: The pestilence has left the realm: no town of Granada is touched any longer. It killed 221,000 of the realm's people, and 52 million across the known world since it rose at Yāyiq. The Black Death has not yet formally ended
source: Trent's screenshot of the Black Death panel

title: The amir comes home from Makka, and from this day he bears the title Ḥājjī. The regency of Faraj ends; word of the pilgrimage has run ahead of the caravan to every Muslim court

data.choice: Let it be known: Makka and back, by grace of Allāh.

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, with the option's tooltip open

title: Home from the Hajj, the amir begins to weigh moving the capital back to Qurṭuba, the old seat of the caliphs
The gravest matter awaiting the amir: a rebellion brewing among the Castilian peasants of the new lands, where the Castilian Patriots have gathered since 1349
source: Trent's account; the rebels appear in the game's panel

title: To head off a rising of the Castilian peasants, the crown offers a concession: the tax on the dhimmīs is lifted for a time. The ʿulamāʾ grumble; the amir doubts it will be enough

data.concession: temporary removal of the dhimmī tax

source: Trent's account (April 1352; the exact day isn't given)
